question:
Solve this question and explain all key methods used 

Let a,b,c>0 satisfy abc=1. Find the minimum value of

\frac{1}{a^2-a+1}+\frac{1}{b^2-b+1}+\frac{1}{c^2-c+1}.

Try solving it first; send your steps and I’ll check them.

slides.title: The constrained expression
slides.caption: S(a,b,c)=\frac{1}{a^2-a+1}+\frac{1}{b^2-b+1}+\frac{1}{c^2-c+1},\qquad a,b,c>0,\qquad abc=1
slides.narration: We study S over positive a, b, and c with product one. The proof has two parts: show S is always above one, then construct values that approach one.

slides.title: Positive denominators
slides.caption: a^2-a+1=\left(a-\frac12\right)^2+\frac34>0
slides.narration: Before comparing fractions, we must know their denominators are positive. Completing the square makes that immediate.

slides.title: A smaller denominator
slides.caption: a^2-a+1<a^2+1\quad(a>0)
slides.narration: Because a is positive, subtracting a from a squared plus one makes the denominator smaller. The same comparison will hold for b and c.

slides.title: Reciprocals reverse
slides.caption: \frac1{a^2-a+1}>\frac1{a^2+1},\qquad \frac1{b^2-b+1}>\frac1{b^2+1},\qquad \frac1{c^2-c+1}>\frac1{c^2+1}
slides.narration: For positive quantities, a smaller denominator produces a larger reciprocal. Applying this term by term gives three strict inequalities.

slides.title: A useful substitution
slides.caption: x=a^2,\qquad y=b^2,\qquad z=c^2,\qquad xyz=(abc)^2=1
slides.narration: The comparison has reduced the problem to denominators of the form one plus a square. Rename those squares x, y, and z. The product constraint becomes xyz=1.

slides.title: Subtracting one
slides.caption: \left(\frac1{1+x}+\frac1{1+y}+\frac1{1+z}\right)-1=\frac{1+x+y+z}{(1+x)(1+y)(1+z)}
slides.narration: Consider the reciprocal sum for x, y, and z. Combining the fractions over a common denominator reveals the amount by which the sum exceeds one.

slides.title: The auxiliary sum exceeds one
slides.caption: \frac1{1+x}+\frac1{1+y}+\frac1{1+z}=1+\frac{1+x+y+z}{(1+x)(1+y)(1+z)}>1
slides.narration: Here x, y, and z are positive. Therefore the displayed remainder is positive, and the reciprocal sum is strictly greater than one.

slides.title: Return to a, b, c
slides.caption: \frac1{1+a^2}+\frac1{1+b^2}+\frac1{1+c^2}>1
slides.narration: Substituting back the squares of a, b, and c gives a strict lower bound for the simpler sum.

slides.title: A strict global bound
slides.caption: S>\frac1{1+a^2}+\frac1{1+b^2}+\frac1{1+c^2}>1
slides.narration: The original expression is strictly larger than the simpler reciprocal sum, and that simpler sum is strictly larger than one. Thus S is always strictly above one.

slides.title: An escaping family
slides.caption: a=b=t,\qquad c=t^{-2},\qquad t>0,\qquad abc=1
slides.narration: To test whether one is the true lower boundary, choose a=b=t and c=t to the power minus two. The product remains exactly one.

slides.title: Evaluate along the family
slides.caption: S(t,t,t^{-2})=\frac{2}{t^2-t+1}+\frac{1}{t^{-4}-t^{-2}+1}
slides.narration: Substitution gives two identical contributions from a and b, while the c-term becomes the expression involving negative powers of t.

slides.title: Approaching the boundary
slides.caption: \lim_{t\to\infty}S(t,t,t^{-2})=\lim_{t\to\infty}\left(\frac{2}{t^2-t+1}+\frac{1}{t^{-4}-t^{-2}+1}\right)=1
slides.narration: As t tends to infinity, the denominator of the first term grows, so that term vanishes. The negative powers in the second denominator vanish, leaving one. The values therefore approach one.

slides.title: Infimum, not minimum
slides.caption: S>1\ \text{for every admissible }(a,b,c),\qquad S(t,t,t^{-2})\to1^+
slides.narration: We have proved S is greater than one for every admissible triple, so one is never attained. But the family gets arbitrarily close to one. Therefore one is the infimum, while no minimum exists.

slides.title: FINAL ANSWER
slides.caption: \boxed{\inf_{a,b,c>0,\,abc=1}\left(\frac1{a^2-a+1}+\frac1{b^2-b+1}+\frac1{c^2-c+1}\right)=1,\qquad \nexists\min}
slides.narration: The expression has infimum one over positive a, b, and c with abc equal to one. Since every value is strictly greater than one, no minimum exists.
